Read a FinalBurn Alpha recording

read_fbm.Rd

Imports FinalBurn Alpha FBM input streams using an explicit game input layout. FBM stores values in driver order, so the recording must be paired with a verified ROM identifier or an ordered schema. Bundled game layouts cite their driver sources in extdata/fbm-layouts.json.

Usage

read_fbm(
  path,
  analog = "raw",
  deadzone = NULL,
  triggers = "raw",
  game = NULL,
  input_schema = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

path

Recording file path.

analog

Stick representation: "raw" (default), "cardinal4", "cardinal8", "angle", or "angle+magnitude". A scalar applies to both sticks; c(left = "cardinal8", right = "angle") selects them independently. Cardinal modes add separate left/right logical direction columns. Continuous modes return numeric fields through stick_channels(). Original X/Y values remain in analog_channels() in every mode. Absent sticks add no columns.

deadzone

Radial threshold in centred axis half-range units, from zero to one. One value applies to both sticks; named left/right values are allowed. NULL uses format defaults: 0.25 for BK2/PSX, 0.125 for M64/DTM. Neutral observations have no direction and an NA angle. Magnitude is kept.

triggers

"raw" (default) or "digital". For DTM, digital additionally projects each analogue trigger at 128/255 into separate L2/R2 columns. Hardware L/R click bits remain distinct from thresholded analogue triggers.

game

A verified ROM identifier matching a bundled input layout, such as "ghouls". Supply either game or input_schema.

input_schema

An ordered schema with a source reference and a fields list. Each field gives key, player (zero for system inputs), type ("button", "byte", or "analog"), and an optional display name. Optional button_encoding is "binary" (default), "bit0", or "nonzero", according to the driver's interpretation of the byte. Field order must match the emulator driver exactly.

...

Reader-specific arguments, such as controller_order for M64 or DTM, or member for a recording inside a ZIP archive (see movie_members()).

Value

A replayr_movie with compact controls and the input schema.

Details

player() returns game controls, analog_channels() retains numeric player inputs, and system_channels() returns cabinet and system inputs. It also retains every raw field under raw_pN_key or raw_system_key, including source bytes whose button interpretation uses only bit zero. Rows follow the stored frame order. The header retains the frame count, rerecord count, source flags, and input-schema reference.

Examples

path <- system.file("extdata", "expanded", "synthetic-arcade.fbm",
                    package = "replayr")
movie <- read_fbm(path, game = "ghouls")
press_counts(movie)
#> Right  Left  Down    Up Start  Fire  Jump 
#>   120    12     0     0     2    12    28
